reported.title: Drip pulses fire back-to-back instead of every 800 ms
reported.description: The scheduler stores the next due time in a uint8_t (line 10) and compares it with a truncated millis() value (lines 63, 71). The condition `(uint8_t)(now8 - nextDue) < 128 && now8 >= nextDue` is satisfied immediately after each pulse ends because nextDue is set to now8+800 which wraps modulo 256, so pulses are emitted roughly every 50 ms rather than 800 ms. Measured evidence shows gaps of 50 ms, 49 ms, 50 ms with 127 of 128 intervals out of tolerance. Expected /^drip$/ every 800 ± 120 ms; 103 of 105 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 705 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Drip solenoid driver on D8; pause button on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Emit a 50 ms HIGH pulse on D8 every 800 ms while pause is released.
- Print the exact line `drip` at the start of each pulse; period must stay 800 ms ±120 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, suppress new pulses and keep D8 LOW.
- Every 1600 ms print `drip n=<count> pause=<0|1>`.
- Stay responsive: complete each pulse without multi-second blocking waits.
